content.thinking: The user asks conceptual physics. No need for tools beyond reasoning. Need answer concise. Explain refrigeration cycle: evaporator coils inside absorb heat from fridge interior via vaporization of refrigerant, compressor raises pressure/temp, condenser coils in back/under fridge release heat to kitchen, expansion valve drops pressure, repeat. content.text:
It moves heat by a vapor-compression cycle: inside the fridge, low-pressure refrigerant evaporates and absorbs heat from the food compartment; a compressor pressurizes and heats it; the hot vapor flows to the condenser coils (usually at the back or underside) where it cools and releases heat to the kitchen; an expansion valve then drops it back to low pressure so it can absorb heat again.

Key point: the fridge expels heat into the kitchen, and because it consumes electricity, it usually makes the room slightly warmer overall. It redistributes and dumps heat; it does not destroy heat like a “refrigerator” does in casual speech.

- “Borrowed Armor” neighborhood heroes: kids pick a cape color, mask, and power; activities include shield decorating, rescue missions, and “save the city” cupcake relay.

content.text:
A hash map is a way to store items so you can find them by a “name” or key, instead of searching through the whole collection one by one.

Think of a dictionary: you look up a word (key) and get its definition (value). A hash map works similarly: you give it a key, and it computes a spot to look for that key, so it usually finds the value very quickly—on average, much faster than scanning everything.

If two keys land in the same spot, that’s called a collision; the map uses rules to handle that. Plain version: **a key-to-value lookup tool designed for fast searching.**
